concerns.text: The cited dataset 'HCP Diffusion/Functional Parquet' (URL: https://huggingface.co/datasets/7eu7d7/HCP-Diffusion-datas/resolve/main/Lexica.art.parquet) appears to be a hallucinated or misnamed artifact. The filename 'Lexica.art.parquet' suggests a connection to the Lexica AI art generator, not the Human Connectome Project (HCP). HCP data is typically distributed as NIfTI images or BIDS-formatted folders, not a single 'Lexica' parquet file. Even if the URL resolves (upstream check), the dataset content is almost certainly inappropriate for deriving structural connectivity matrices and fMRI time series. The plan assumes this file contains 'Structural matrices, fMRI time series' without evidence. This is a wrong-dataset-for-the-question failure.

The second cited source 'HCP Train Split' (URL: https://huggingface.co/datasets/ramandeepsaha/hcp/resolve/main/train.csv) is a generic user-uploaded dataset on Hugging Face with no official HCP provenance. It is unlikely to contain the raw dMRI/fMRI data required for the pipeline (FR-001, FR-002). The plan treats this as a 'Verified source' for 'Structural matrices, fMRI time series', but the URL points to a CSV likely containing only metadata or a tiny subset. Relying on this for the primary data acquisition (Phase 0) will result in missing data or schema mismatches, breaking the pipeline.

The third cited source 'HCP Flat Data' (URL: https://huggingface.co/datasets/jonxuxu/HCP-flat/resolve/main/data/train-00000-of-00001-ecc38ed386fa0d8c.parquet) is similarly an unverified, user-generated repository. The plan claims it contains 'Flattened connectivity matrices', but without an official HCP accession ID (e.g., ds000224 on OpenNeuro) or a link to the official HCP data portal, the validity of the data modality and quality cannot be guaranteed. The plan's assumption that these three specific Hugging Face user-uploads contain the necessary high-quality dMRI and fMRI data for 50 subjects is methodologically unsound.
